claims.text: The nanoparticles are equimolar PtPdNiCuCo high-entropy alloys.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneous solid solutions with uniformly distributed metal atoms.
A sufficiently high average diffusion activation energy suppresses significant atomic diffusion over 473–1923 K.
Suppressing significant atomic diffusion maintains the structural and chemical stability of the solid solution.
A constituent with a notably lower diffusion barrier will diffuse more rapidly at elevated temperature.
Enhanced diffusion of a low-barrier constituent triggers local compositional segregation, including clustering or core-shell formation.
Local compositional segregation degrades catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Local atomic diffusion barriers govern the kinetic stability of the nanoparticles.
Local diffusion barriers underlie the entropic stabilization of the high-entropy alloy.
When the composite average diffusion activation energy exceeds the available thermal energy, the solid solution remains kinetically locked.
A constituent with a significantly lower diffusion barrier can initiate diffusion even at moderate thermal energies.
Nanoparticles whose constituents all have uniformly high diffusion activation energies will largely retain their homogeneous solid solution and performance in inert and mildly oxidizing environments.
The presence of any constituent with a notably lower diffusion barrier will produce early phase segregation or ordering.
The predicted segregation or ordering will be accompanied by a measurable decline in catalytic or thermoelectric performance relative to the initial state.
Catalytic and thermoelectric performance is optimal in the initial equimolar homogeneous solid-solution state.
Oxidation and electron-beam artifacts can confound interpretation of high-temperature diffusion and segregation.
In-situ TEM/EDS, atom-probe tomography, and synchrotron measurements can quantify diffusion profiles, local activation energies, and segregation in these nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The stability criterion alternates between a high composite-average activation energy and the absence of any low-barrier constituent. A particle could have a high average barrier while still containing one low-barrier metal, so the governing criterion is internally ambiguous.

The design specifies only identically synthesized PtPdNiCuCo nanoparticles, whereas the falsification rule requires a comparison between particles expected to have uniformly high barriers and particles with known lower barriers. Those comparison cohorts are not defined in the design.
